name: Losar
summary: Losar is the Tibetan new year, celebrated in Darjeeling's Buddhist monasteries and homes over several days in February or March. Ghum's Yiga Choeling and the town's Tibetan and Bhutia families mark it with prayers, butter lamps, fresh prayer flags and new-year food.
body: Losar falls on the first day of the Tibetan lunar calendar, usually in February and sometimes in early March. In the Darjeeling hills it belongs to the Tibetan, Bhutia, Sherpa, Tamang and other Buddhist communities. In the days before, houses are cleaned, debts settled and old prayer flags replaced. The day before the new year, many families eat guthuk, a noodle soup with dough balls holding small tokens.

On the morning of Losar, families visit monasteries with offerings. Ghum's Yiga Choeling, founded in 1850, and other monasteries around Ghum and Darjeeling fill with butter lamps and visitors, and monks hold special prayers. Some monasteries perform masked cham dances around this time, though the exact dates differ by monastery and tradition, so ask locally.

For visitors, Losar is a chance to see the hills' Buddhist life at its most open. Expect crowds at the monasteries in the morning, closed shops in Tibetan neighbourhoods on the first days, and plenty of khapse, the fried new-year biscuits, being shared. It is also low season for tourism, so hotel rates are often lower.
tips: Check the Losar date for your year early; it moves with the lunar calendar and Sonam Losar or Gyalpo Losar dates differ.
Walk clockwise around monasteries and stupas, and ask before photographing prayers or people.
Pack for cold: Ghum at 2,258 m is often 0–6 °C and foggy in February.

faqs.q: When is Losar celebrated in Darjeeling
faqs.a: Losar follows the Tibetan lunar calendar and usually falls in February, sometimes early March. Celebrations run over several days, with the main monastery visits on the first day. The Tamang community also marks Sonam Losar, usually a few weeks earlier. Check the exact date for your year before you travel, as it changes every year.

faqs.q: Can tourists visit monasteries during Losar
faqs.a: Yes. Monasteries such as Yiga Choeling in Ghum stay open, and visitors are welcome if they are respectful. Go in the morning, dress warmly and modestly, remove shoes where asked, and do not walk in front of people praying. Ask before taking photos inside prayer halls, and keep phones on silent.

faqs.q: What food is eaten at Losar in Darjeeling
faqs.a: Families make guthuk, a noodle soup eaten the night before the new year, and khapse, fried biscuits shaped in twists and knots. Momos, thukpa and butter tea appear on most tables. Some Tibetan restaurants close for a day or two, so check opening times around the festival.

faqs.q: Is February a good time to visit Darjeeling for Losar
faqs.a: It is a good, cheap time if you can handle the cold. February is off-season, so hotel rates are lower and roads are quieter. Days can be clear, but nights drop near freezing and Ghum is often in fog. Pack thermals, gloves and a warm hat.

name: Saga Dawa and Buddha Jayanti
when: May–Jun, full moon of the fourth Tibetan month
summary: Saga Dawa marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing. In Darjeeling, monasteries hold prayers through the month, and on the full-moon day monks and families walk in procession through town carrying scriptures and statues, with music from long horns and cymbals.
body: Saga Dawa is the fourth month of the Tibetan calendar, held as the holiest month of the Buddhist year. Its full-moon day, Saga Dawa Duchen, marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing into nirvana, and it overlaps with the Buddha Purnima holiday observed across India. The date falls in May or June.

In Darjeeling, the day is marked by a procession that winds through the town from the monasteries, with monks in maroon robes, long dungchen horns, cymbals and drums, and lay people carrying sacred texts and images. Families light butter lamps, give to charity and avoid eating meat, because good deeds done this month are believed to be multiplied many times.

For visitors it is one of the most open and moving days in the hills. May is also peak tourist season, so the town is full and hotel rates are high. Find a place along the route early, step aside for the procession, and do not cut through the line of monks for a photograph.
tips: Ask your hotel or the nearest monastery the night before for the procession route and start time.
Book rooms early: Saga Dawa falls in peak season, when rates are at their highest.
Carry a light rain jacket, as pre-monsoon showers are common by late May.

faqs.q: When is Buddha Jayanti in Darjeeling
faqs.a: It falls on the full moon of the fourth Tibetan month, Saga Dawa, usually in May and occasionally in early June. The date changes every year with the lunar calendar. Monasteries hold prayers through the month, and the main procession happens on the full-moon day. Check current dates before you travel.

faqs.q: Where does the Buddha Jayanti procession go in Darjeeling
faqs.a: The procession usually starts from the monasteries and passes through the main roads of town, including the area around Chowrasta and the Mall. The exact route can change from year to year. Ask at your hotel or a monastery the evening before, and find a spot early because the roads fill up.

faqs.q: Can tourists join the Saga Dawa celebrations
faqs.a: Visitors are welcome to watch and to visit monasteries during Saga Dawa. Dress modestly, stand aside to let the procession pass, and ask before photographing people at prayer. Many locals avoid meat this month, and some restaurants serve only vegetarian food on the full-moon day.

faqs.q: Is May a good month to visit Darjeeling
faqs.a: May is peak season: warm days of 12–19 °C, rhododendrons on the high ridges and busy hotels. Mountain views are less reliable than in October and November because of haze and pre-monsoon cloud. If you come for Saga Dawa, book stays and cars at least four to six weeks ahead.

name: Dashain
when: Sep–Oct, ten days ending on Vijaya Dashami
summary: Dashain is the biggest festival of the Gorkha and Nepali-speaking families who make up most of the Darjeeling hills. It runs for fifteen days around the Durga Puja season, with the main day, Tika, when elders place red tika and jamara barley shoots on the foreheads of the young.
body: Dashain celebrates the victory of the goddess Durga over evil and runs alongside Bengal's Durga Puja, but in the hills it has its own rhythm and food. It begins on Ghatasthapana, when jamara, barley seeds, are sown in a dark corner of the house. On the tenth day, Vijaya Dashami, families gather and elders bless the younger ones with tika, a paste of rice, curd and red colour, and tuck the yellow jamara shoots behind their ears.

Families travel back from Siliguri, Kolkata and beyond, so the shared jeeps fill and the town has a holiday feel. Homes cook goat meat, sel roti and other festive dishes, and bamboo swings called ping are put up in some villages. Shops may close for the main days, and many drivers take leave.

For travellers, Dashain overlaps with the start of the clear autumn season and with the Puja holidays, the busiest time of the year for visitors from Kolkata. Book rooms, cars and train seats as early as you can, and expect higher prices. In return you see the hills at their most festive.
tips: Book NJP train seats and hill rooms as soon as Puja dates are announced; this is the busiest fortnight of the year.
Arrange your car in advance: many drivers take leave around Tika day.
If a family offers tika and a sweet, accept with both hands; it is a blessing, not a show.

faqs.q: When is Dashain celebrated in Darjeeling
faqs.a: Dashain falls in late September or October, following the lunar calendar, and lasts about fifteen days. The main day, Vijaya Dashami or Tika, coincides with Bijoya Dashami of Bengal's Durga Puja. Check the dates for your year before you travel, as hotel prices and transport depend heavily on them.

faqs.q: Is it a good idea to visit Darjeeling during Dashain and Durga Puja
faqs.a: It is festive and often clear, but it is the busiest and most expensive time of year. Rooms, train seats and cars sell out weeks ahead, and some shops and drivers stop work around Tika day. Book early, or come a week after the main days, when the weather is still good and crowds ease.

faqs.q: What is jamara in Dashain
faqs.a: Jamara are barley shoots grown in the dark for nine days from the first day of Dashain, so they come up pale yellow. On Tika day, elders place them on the heads or behind the ears of younger family members along with the red rice tika, as a blessing for the year ahead.

faqs.q: Do shops and transport close during Dashain in Darjeeling
faqs.a: Some do, especially on and around Tika day, when families stay home. Shared jeeps run but fill quickly with people travelling home, and fares can rise. Reserve your car in advance and keep a little cash in hand, because some ATMs run dry over the long holiday.

name: Tihar
summary: Tihar is the five-day festival of lights of the hills, held at Diwali. Each day honours a different being: crows, dogs, cows, then oneself, and finally brothers on Bhai Tika. Houses glow with lamps and marigold garlands, and groups go door to door singing Deusi and Bhailo.
body: Tihar arrives about two weeks after Dashain and runs for five days. The first day honours crows, which are fed at dawn. The second, Kukur Tihar, honours dogs, and you will see the town's dogs wearing marigold garlands and red tika. The third day honours the cow and Laxmi, goddess of wealth, and houses are lit with oil lamps and electric lights.

On the evenings of Tihar, groups of young people go from house to house singing Bhailo and Deusi songs, receiving money, sweets and sel roti in return. The last day, Bhai Tika, is for brothers and sisters: sisters give their brothers a seven-coloured tika and garlands of makhamali flowers, and brothers give gifts in return.

For visitors, Tihar is the prettiest week in the hills. The air is usually clear, Kangchenjunga is often visible in the mornings, and the town glows at night. It is still busy season, so book ahead, and expect some shops to close on Bhai Tika.
tips: Walk the lanes below Chowrasta after dark on the third evening, when houses are lit for Laxmi Puja.
If Deusi singers come to your homestay, a small gift of ₹100–200 is the custom.
Do not feed street dogs on Kukur Tihar unless locals invite you; garlanded dogs can be overwhelmed.

faqs.q: When is Tihar in Darjeeling
faqs.a: Tihar falls at Diwali, usually in late October or November, and lasts five days. It follows the lunar calendar, so the dates change every year. The busiest evenings are the third day, Laxmi Puja, and the last day, Bhai Tika. Check the exact dates before you travel.

faqs.q: What is Kukur Tihar
faqs.a: Kukur Tihar is the second day of Tihar, when dogs are honoured. Families and shopkeepers put red tika on their dogs' foreheads, garland them with marigolds and give them good food. In Darjeeling you will see the town's street and pet dogs wearing garlands all day. It is a real custom, not a tourist show.

faqs.q: What are Deusi and Bhailo
faqs.a: Deusi and Bhailo are songs sung door to door during Tihar. Girls traditionally sing Bhailo and boys sing Deusi, though mixed groups are common now. Households give money, fruit, sweets and sel roti in return. In homestays the singers may arrive late in the evening, and guests often join in.

faqs.q: Is Darjeeling crowded during Diwali
faqs.a: Yes, Diwali week is busy, especially with travellers from Kolkata and Siliguri, and hotel prices are high. It is also one of the best weeks for clear morning views. Book rooms and cars two to four weeks ahead, and plan sightseeing early in the day to stay ahead of the traffic.

name: Ghum Festival of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
image_query: Ghum railway station Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
when: Late Nov–early Dec (2026 edition planned 28 Nov–6 Dec)
summary: An annual festival run by the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway around Ghum, India's highest railway station, marking the line's UNESCO listing in December 1999. Recent editions have included a heritage run from Chowrasta to Ghum, music, literature events in Kurseong and special train rides.
body: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway was added to UNESCO's World Heritage List in December 1999. The railway now marks that anniversary with the Ghum Festival, centred on Ghum station at 2,258 metres, the highest on India's railways, with its small museum of old engines, tickets and photographs.

The 2025 edition ran from 2 to 10 December. It included the Iron Sherpa Heritage Run, in which nearly 200 runners raced from Chowrasta to Ghum station, the Kurseong Literature Festival, the DHRUMA music festival and performances on open-roofed trains. The railway has said the next edition will run from 28 November to 6 December 2026.

Events change from year to year, and dates can move, so treat this as a guide and check current status before you travel. Early December is also a fine time for the hills: the air is clear and cold, Kangchenjunga is often visible, and hotel rates fall after the Diwali rush.
tips: Watch the Northeast Frontier Railway and DHR announcements in November for the final programme.
Book joyride seats on IRCTC early; festival weekends sell out.
Dress for 2–8 °C at Ghum, colder after dark and in fog.

faqs.q: When is the Ghum Festival held
faqs.a: It is held around early December to mark the DHR's UNESCO listing in December 1999. The 2025 edition ran 2–10 December, and the railway announced 28 November to 6 December for 2026. Dates and events can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What happens at the Ghum Festival
faqs.a: Recent editions have included the Iron Sherpa Heritage Run from Chowrasta to Ghum station, music, literature events in Kurseong and performances on open-roofed trains. The museum at Ghum station is open, and special joyrides often run. The programme changes each year, so look for the final schedule in November.

faqs.q: Is December a good time to visit Darjeeling
faqs.a: Yes, for clear views and lower prices. Days are around 6–12 °C and nights near freezing, but skies are often clean, and Kangchenjunga shows on most mornings. Crowds return around Christmas and New Year, so early December is the sweet spot for value.

faqs.q: How do I reach Ghum station from Darjeeling
faqs.a: Ghum is about 7 km from Darjeeling by road, 20–30 minutes by shared jeep or taxi, or about 40 minutes on the toy train, which also stops at Batasia Loop on joyrides. Shared jeeps towards Ghum and Sukhiapokhri cost around ₹30–60 a seat, indicative 2026.
